obernants.observation_scope: Values, shape, errors and named assertions
obernants.operator: Within validated calls and candidate coefficients, incompatible recurrences or a compatible recurrence of nonminimal order are absent. Invalid over-cap calls paired with Ok are absent. Compatibility/minimality alone is an outer description of possible output: deterministic tie choice imposes extra constraints.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations

obernants.observation_scope: Values, shape, errors and named assertions
obernants.operator: For observed c, retain all prefixes whose deterministic discrepancy schedule returns c. The looser algebraic fiber contains every prefix compatible with c and no shorter order, but may include prefixes selecting another tie. All-zero prefixes of every admissible length share empty output; uniqueness is absent.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations

obernants.observation_scope: Values, shape, errors and named assertions
obernants.operator: For candidate order k form rows (s[t-1],...,s[t-k]|s[t]) for k<=t<n. Feasibility is rank(A)=rank(A|b); returned L is the least feasible k. Gaussian rank is an independent finite oracle; it neither identifies future terms nor claims uniqueness.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations

obernants.operator: Prefix [1,2,3] has minimum order2 and admits [1,1] and [0,3], predicting5 and6 respectively at the next position. A chosen recurrence is a compatible continuation, not inference of a uniquely determined infinite source.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations

obernants.operator: Return c[j]=-connection[j+1] modulo p so c[0] multiplies the immediately previous term. For positive L use initial=s[..L] with linear_recurrence::nth_term and modulus p. Empty L must be handled separately because nth_term rejects empty order.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations

obernants.observation_scope: Values, shape, errors and named assertions
obernants.operator: Every saved previous discrepancy is nonzero and p=998244353 is prime, so previous^(p-2) is its inverse. Composite or caller-selected moduli are outside this API. Zero discrepancy performs no inversion and only increments shift.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations

obernants.observation_scope: Values, shape, errors and named assertions
obernants.operator: All raw u64 values are reduced before multiplication. For p=998244353, (p-1)^2<2^60; multiplication fits u64, and addition/subtraction intermediates are below2p. With n<=4096, n+1,2L and shifts fit usize. Congruent representatives yield identical output.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations

obernants.observation_scope: Values, shape, errors and named assertions
obernants.operator: n>4096 returns TooManyTerms before any allocation; otherwise fallible reservations can return AllocationFailed. Empty prefixes still allocate connection arrays and may fail allocation. No allocator-failure injection or memory exhaustion guarantee is claimed.
obernants.assumptions: Prime field, declared resource domain and successful allocations
